steps.content: [Truth Declassified] Documentary

steps.speaker: Newscast
steps.content: In N.F. 115, DisCity has taken the decisive step of unveiling the long-concealed BR-003 to the public—a direct response to the aggressive Tide of Ashes launched by the farlands.

steps.speaker: Newscast
steps.content: As the optical camouflage dissolved, we witnessed the ultimate deterrent against humanity's most belligerent extremists, as well as the embodiment of DisCity's extraordinary efforts to suppress and relocate BR-003.

steps.speaker: Newscast
steps.content: Newly declassified documents now offer a glimpse into the prolonged city-state conflicts that have remained shrouded in secrecy.

steps.speaker: Newscast
steps.content: From previously released information, we know that in N.F. 106, DisCity hosted the 12th Great Expo. At that time, the observatory still stood on the surface, serving as a symbol of hope that this marvel beneath the stars might help mend the fractures between city-states.

steps.speaker: Newscast
steps.content: But that hope was shattered. During the exhibition, Mania extremists attempted to spread contamination, ultimately triggering BR-003 on site. The catastrophe claimed thousands of lives and shattered a fragile peace.

steps.speaker: Newscast
steps.content: At that time, humanity lacked the means to suppress the Black Rings. The mental corruption caused by hazardous information was irreversible. To protect the public, DisCity concealed the existence of BR-003, limited the release of information about the tragedy, and intensified its crackdown on Mania.

steps.speaker: Newscast
steps.content: For years, we were led to believe it was solely the work of Mania extremists. But now, with war once again at our doorstep, a more alarming possibility emerges: that the Outlands and the Underground Maniacs had already formed an alliance.

steps.speaker: Newscast
steps.content: They saw their opportunity in N.F. 103, the year FAC was crippled by the Eclipse Operation, and the last of the DisCorps forces had withdrawn. They believed it was the perfect moment to break DisCity apart and overthrow the established order.

steps.speaker: Newscast
steps.content: They failed then. And they will fail now. Because though DisCity's defenders may have been absent from public view, their loyalty never wavered. They've been vigilantly operating beyond our borders, guarding against external threats.

steps.speaker: Newscast
steps.content: Now, they have returned. And with them, we reclaim our strength, confront our history, and secure the future of our city-state...

steps.speaker: Panicked Civilian
steps.content: It hurts... It's burning hot... Help me...

steps.speaker: Panicked Civilian
steps.content: Why is this happening... hnngh... WAAAHH—
[Transition: Mimic TV Channel Change/TikTok Swipe] Sound effect, black screen

steps.speaker: EDGE-03
steps.content: If we had any other choice, we wouldn't take such drastic measures. But this war... it must end now.
[Transition: Syndicate Streets] Add TV static

steps.speaker: Max King
steps.content: Stay calm, everyone! The Speaker of the City Council is here! Your Max King has arrived with everything you need!
[Power Off] Sound effect: THUD— head smashing into screen

steps.speaker: Max King
steps.content: What the hell is this about?!
As he scrolls through a stream of videos, Speaker Max King comes face-to-face with his own image, and nearly hurls his terminal across the room in rage.

August 14, N.F. 115 15:00
West District Temporary Underground Defense Works
A fragile, three-day stalemate has held since EDGE's declaration on August 11th.

Though direct conflict has paused, the farlands' Tide of Ashes refuses to recede, blocking vital shipping routes. In response, DisCity has cranked its propaganda engine to full capacity, pushing the amended mobilization order into a second round of debate.
The message is clear: beneath the quiet, both sides are preparing, probing defenses, and gathering strength. Neither has any intention of stopping.

It all leaves Max King sick with frustration, a feeling he feeds by obsessively checking the very news that demoralizes him. Like now, he anonymously logs into a popular forum where the war has ignited a firestorm of speculation and fear.

<color=#fb9259>Outlanders</color><size=28> are all </size><color=#fb9259><size=52>butchers</color></size>. The more brutal we are, the better.
My cousin just enlisted <color=#fb9259><size=45>yesterday</color></size>. Says he's not afraid, <size=28>but I'm terrified for him...</size>
<color=#fb9259><size=52>Peace</color></size> talks are a joke. <color=#fb9259>Kill</color> all those Outland mutts!
The <color=#fb9259><size=45>FAC's</color><size=28> just a bunch of losers</size>. All this time and no real progress...

And then there's the deadweight <color=#fb9259><size=52>West District</color></size>!
The <color=#fb9259>new mobilization order</color> is REAL. They're literally grabbing people off the street into trucks rn. <size=28>If you don't wanna die, </size><color=#fb9259>STAY INSIDE</color>.
So easy for people to scream for war when <color=#fb9259><size=45>it's not their family on the front lines</color></size>.
<size=28>All these </size><color=#fb9259>armchair</color> generals <size=45>should be the first ones handed a rifle!</size>
<color=#fb9259><size=52>This is crazy! Actual madness!</color></size>

OMG the new <size=52>EDGE</size> <color=#fb9259>weapon</color> is terrifying. <size=28>That'll shut people up.</size>
But the <color=#fb9259><size=45>Tide of Ashes</color></size> is still there... so the <color=#fb9259>Outlanders</color> haven't really backed down, right?
How long until this <color=#fb9259>"ceasefire"</color><size=28> falls apart</size>? Bet they're back at it by <color=#fb9259>tomorrow</color>.
LOL it's the same story <color=#fb9259><size=52>every time</color></size>. <color=#fb9259>Ceasefire on paper</color>, fighting by morning.

I just wish we had <color=#fb9259><size=45>a real leader</color></size> who could actually <color=#fb9259><size=52>win</color></size> this thing...
<color=#fb9259><size=45>Max King</color></size>? What's he done? Can he stop <color=#fb9259>playing clown</color> online and actually do something?!
<color=#fb9259><size=45>...How much longer will this go on? My stash is running low.</color></size>

Okay, so one of my relatives does supply runs to <color=#fb9259>Paradeisos</color> and gave me some <color=#fb9259>legit</color> tea:
That <color=#fb9259>big thing in the sky</color> is a distraction... The real power move is the <color=#fb9259>DisCorps! Those psychos</color> are coming back!

Wait, <color=#fb9259><size=52>for real</color></size>?? That sounds like crap. Got any proof? Source: trust me bro?
...Okay but lowkey they might be onto something. I saw some soldiers in weird, old-school <color=#fb9259>uniforms</color> the other day. Apparently not the FAC's.
<color=#fb9259><size=45>Seriously?? Spill the beans!!</color></size>

I heard they're the reason WhiteSands became a <color=#fb9259>bloodbath</color> back in the day!
If <color=#fb9259>they</color> are really stepping in, the Outlands are so screwed.
See? This is what we need. The <color=#fb9259>old guards</color> know how to get stuff done.

But hello?? Remember they were all <color=#fb9259>insane</color>... Aren't we just trading one nightmare for another?
You think they <color=#fb9259><size=45>care</color></size> if we live or die? Don't be so naive! <size=28>In their era, we were just </size><color=#fb9259>numbers</color> to them.

IDGAF, I'm all for <color=#fb9259><size=45>DisCorps</color></size>. We need an <color=#fb9259>iron fist</color> right now.
<size=28>Yo I heard Dravyn didn't kill himself... she iced him?</size>
This is a golden opportunity! Why aren't we grabbing it?! Are you people crazy?!
<color=#fb9259><size=28>I don't care who's in charge, just stop using us as cannon fodder...</color></size>

lol why is everyone so stressed? <color=#fb9259>It's fiiine</color>. Just be happy we can still post our nonsense online.
Who knows which one of us is gonna get <color=#fb9259><size=52>perma-logged off</color></size> next, heh.
<size=28>Will it be a catastrophe, a Black Ring, or DisCorps that gets us? </size><color=#fb9259>Same diff in the end</color>...
Reaching his limit, he fumbles for his phone to make the call he's always been cautious about, but someone arrives before he can—

steps.speaker: Secretary
steps.content: Is there something you need, Mr. Speaker? If you need to reach someone, I can handle that for you.

steps.speaker: Max King
steps.content: Do you really have to watch my every move?

steps.speaker: Secretary
steps.content: I'm afraid so, sir. These are extraordinary times. I need to stay on top of your schedule. Please don't hesitate to tell me what you need arranged.
Her meaning is perfectly clear to Max King. She is less an assistant and more a warden, her true purpose to monitor him and preempt any unsanctioned actions.
Apparently, his gut response to the last "directive" has been a mistake, eroding their trust and triggering this increased scrutiny from EDGE.

Is it his aggression in the council? A slip of the mask when he dealt with Nirvana during the Great Expo? Or is this always his destiny, to be the outsider who finally reached the inner circle only to find a locked door?
Looming over it all is the enigma of EDGE itself...
[Enter Flashback]

steps.speaker: Elvira
steps.content: Public intel on EDGE is practically nonexistent. They have all this authority and all these secrets, but they also operate under a really strict, self-imposed code. Their ability to "guide" humanity is actually very limited.

steps.speaker: Elvira
steps.content: I heard that the scientists who founded E.D.G.E. set it up that way. And the original members were all scientists.

steps.speaker: Elvira
steps.content: But as years went by, the members changed. The group's makeup got more complex. Where they come from, in what areas and under what pretext they "guide" humanity, how members relate to each other... it's all a mystery now.
[Exit Flashback]
The invisible grip around his neck tightens again, stealing his words. Max King falls silent as he slowly puts away his terminal.

steps.speaker: Max King
steps.content: I need to get through to the MBCC.

steps.speaker: Max King
steps.content: Look at the West District. It's a powder keg. If this continues, we'll have a full-scale catastrophe on our hands. Chief ${PlayerName} has the capability and respect to get ahead of this. I need his support.
steps.female_content: Look at the West District. It's a powder keg. If this continues, we'll have a full-scale catastrophe on our hands. Chief ${PlayerName} has the capability and respect to get ahead of this. I need her support.

steps.speaker: Secretary
steps.content: Sir, as I've said, Chief ${PlayerName}'s condition has taken a turn. Right now the Chief is being treated at the best sanatorium in Eastside and cannot leave at the moment.

steps.speaker: Max King
steps.content: Why there? Why not the MBCC? Or Banyan? Sending the Chief so far away makes no sense.

steps.speaker: Secretary
steps.content: We're living in extraordinary times. For someone of Chief ${PlayerName}'s stature, we must take every precaution. We can't be too careful with his security.
steps.female_content: We're living in extraordinary times. For someone of Chief ${PlayerName}'s stature, we must take every precaution. We can't be too careful with her security.

steps.speaker: Max King
steps.content: ...If it's that serious, then I need to see him. ${PlayerName} is a crucial asset to this city. And he's a friend. I should be there for him when he's having a rough time.
steps.female_content: ...If it's that serious, then I need to see her. ${PlayerName} is a crucial asset to this city. And she's a friend. I should be there for her when she's having a rough time.

steps.speaker: Secretary
steps.content: I'm afraid the doctors are insisting on absolute rest. No visitors. If you have a message, I can see that it's delivered.

steps.speaker: Secretary
steps.content: Besides, you're quite busy with your own affairs, aren't you? EDGE needs you in front of the cameras, keeping up morale.
A moment of silence falls.

steps.speaker: Max King
steps.content: ...Morale. What is any of this pageantry actually accomplishing?
Suppression, ridicule, surveillance—these threats leave him cold. They cannot touch him.
What truly torments Max King is his own powerlessness, a bitter truth underscored in moments like this one.
And so, no matter how deep his reluctance, the Speaker of the City Council allows himself to be "escorted" back to the cameras by the secretary's smiling, inescapable presence.
[Black Screen]
[Scene Change] Confinement Cell
Night falls. The interrogations have ended, and for a brief moment, Selyna's cell is left unguarded.
But she remains locked in the most severe form of anti-Mania restraint. Pain has made sleep nearly impossible, and at the sound of approaching footsteps, her eyes snap open.

steps.speaker: Selyna
steps.content: Who's there?!

steps.speaker: Selyna
steps.content: DisCity dogs... you come to kill me? Go ahead!!!

Standing before her is a frail, pale girl—utterly ordinary, with no discernible power or killing intent. She looks harmless; back in Selyna's homeland, someone like her would have been assigned to production duty, far from the front lines.

steps.speaker: Elvira
steps.content: ...Selyna?
Her hand shakes, but she still reaches for the control panel and slightly lowers the suppression frequency.

steps.speaker: Elvira
steps.content: ...I'm not a guard here. I'm not here to kill you, but I can't set you free either. I just thought... you shouldn't have gone through all this pain.
Then Selyna notices the girl's elaborate clothing—the unmistakable style of a DisCity socialite, something she's seen in intelligence reports. Rage flares in the farland warrior's eyes.

steps.speaker: Selyna
steps.content: Don't think I'll fall for your tricks! Go to hell!!!
The silver-haired girl opens her mouth as if to speak, bites her lower lip, and eventually takes a step back.

steps.speaker: Elvira
steps.content: You don't have to be so hostile. I just... don't want to see an Outlander die like this.
Having mustered the courage to speak, she turns quickly and leaves, head lowered, leaving Selyna alone in confusion.
[Scene Change] El Exits the Corridor

Elvira slips away from the detention area, the special access card hidden in her palm as she steals back into the regular zone. Her heart still hammers against her ribs. So far, no one at MBCC has noticed her.
After all, the entire facility is in chaos right now.
[MBCC] Lounge

After EDGE declared a state of emergency, ${PlayerName} was taken away, officially for a health examination. But Elvira knows better. It is house arrest. Whether because he's in someone's way or simply deemed too unpredictable, the result is the same.
steps.female_content: After EDGE declared a state of emergency, ${PlayerName} was taken away, officially for a health examination. But Elvira knows better. It is house arrest. Whether because she's in someone's way or simply deemed too unpredictable, the result is the same.

steps.content: Without ${PlayerName}, MBCC has turned isolated and restricted, its internal flow of information choked off.

Elvira herself is also under surveillance. She needs more—intelligence that can bypass the Bureau's constraints, something beyond what Stewart's inheritance offered. She needs newer, wider sources. But she can't do it alone, not when trapped here.
What can she do...?

steps.speaker: Max King
steps.content: Stay calm, everyone! The Speaker of the City Council is here! Your Max King has arrived with everything you need!
The noise from the Recreation Area breaks through her thoughts. Elvira halts mid-step. The television is still on, and a familiar face flashes across the screen.
The absurd performance draws laughter from the crowd gathered around. Under all this tension, everyone needs a distraction.

steps.speaker: Elvira
steps.content: ...He's really bad at acting...
And yet... the spectacle gives her an idea.
[Scene Change] MBCC Corridor (or Witching Hour Underground Parking Garage)
In the MBCC's underground garage, a transport team from the West District delivers a new group of Sinners contaminated by the shackles to Nightingale.

steps.speaker: West District Staff Member
steps.content: That's the last of them. We gotta go. There are still a lot of people back in the West District who need medical attention.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: Understood. Leave the Sinners to MBCC. We're counting on you over there in the West District.
With a crisp salute, the staff member turns and hurries back to his companion.

steps.speaker: West District Staff Member
steps.content: Let's hurry. We're short-handed as it is, we've gotta get back— Hm? Who are you?
An unfamiliar girl grabs his sleeve. She looks up at him, her expression timid.

steps.speaker: Elvira
steps.content: Please... let me come with you. I can help.

steps.speaker: West District Staff Member
steps.content: ...But your hands are shaking.
The West District has been ravaged by the Tide of Ashes—or rather, by the war it represents. Elvira reads the thought in his eyes: He can't let a child go there in a time like this.
The fear she feels is raw and real, far beyond the reach of her acting. For once, she lets it show.

steps.speaker: Elvira
steps.content: I'm sorry, I lied... My dad works at the Bureau, but my mom... she's stationed in the West District. I'm just... really worried about her.

steps.speaker: Elvira
steps.content: Can you take me to her?
